source_documents.title: A Solid-State-Emissive 1,8-Naphthalimide Probe Based on Photoinduced Electron Transfer and Aggregation-Induced Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: In this work we focused on the design and synthesis of a fluorescence sensing 4-chloro-1,8-naptalimide derivative operating simultaneously by photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and aggregation induced emission (AIE) mechanisms.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probe 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Designed as PET plus AIE sensor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The photoinduced fluorescence enhancement of the probe was FE = 22 after protonation in solution
reference_evidence_units.subject: probe 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonating the amine receptor turns emission on 22-fold.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In solid state on paper support the PET process in the probe was switched “off” in a pH window 2.5-1.5.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probe 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET switching also in the solid.

reference_evidence_units.quote: in concentrated solutions the new compound 1 displayed a well pronounced green AIE fluorescence (Figure S5) centred at 525 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: probe 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: A red-shifted aggregate band (525 nm vs 405 nm monomer).
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Origin of the aggregate band not analysed.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Fluorophore-spacer-receptor PET probe: protonation of the amine blocks PET and turns emission on.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Aggregates show a separate red-shifted green band; the paper calls it AIE without assigning a mechanism.
